writing.overall_comment: A well-scoped and safety-conscious skill whose high-level principles are strong, but it would benefit from more realistic, correct command examples and explicit failure-recovery paths in the main document.

dimensions.name: Semantic accuracy
dimensions.comment: The name and description accurately reflect the skill's scope (interactive rebase, worktree, reflog, bisect, commit conventions, history cleanup), and the body stays consistent with that promise.

dimensions.name: Examples & edge cases
dimensions.comment: The bash snippets are mostly correct but thin and partly unreliable (e.g., `git reflog | grep "commit message"` and a bare `git reset --hard` after locating a lost commit), and no failure paths such as rebase conflicts, failed bisect, or unrecoverable reflog expiry are demonstrated.

dimensions.name: Actionability
dimensions.comment: Core commands and the safety ordering (reflog → backup branch → recover) are explicit and executable, but several steps lack verification/rollback detail and the substantive guidance lives only in unshown reference files.
